intended_object: The canonical group isomorphism Ext^n(X, Y) ≅ H^n(Hom(P•, Y)) for a projective resolution P• → X: Ext computed as cohomology classes of degree-n cochain maps from the resolution to Y placed in degree 0. Inferred from the docstring and the module's purpose ("Computing Ext using a projective resolution").
explanation:
The body takes the existing bijection `extEquivCohomologyClass` and adds the proof (`extEquivCohomologyClass_symm_add`) that it respects addition, so it becomes an `AddEquiv`. That bijection is built in two steps. First, precompose with the quasi-isomorphism `R.π'` from the resolution to `X`, which identifies shifted morphisms out of `X` with shifted morphisms out of `R.cochainComplex`. Second, use the K-projectivity of the resolution (`equivOfIsKProjective`) to identify those with cohomology classes of the Hom complex. This is the standard identification Ext^n(X, Y) ≅ H^n(Hom(P•, Y)).

The generality is the usual one: any abelian category with `HasExt`, any projective resolution, any n. A more general version for arbitrary K-projective complexes already exists separately (`CohomologyClass.equivOfIsKProjective`); this declaration is the specialisation to projective resolutions, which is exactly what the docstring says it is.

This declaration is the additive upgrade of `extEquivCohomologyClass` in the same file. There is no other Mathlib declaration of this additive isomorphism, so the counterpart field is left empty.
